title: Cross Product of Two Vectors
notes: **Definition.** a × b = |a||b| sin θ n̂, with n̂ given by the right-hand rule; in components a × b = (a₂b₃ − a₃b₂, a₃b₁ − a₁b₃, a₁b₂ − a₂b₁).
**Determinant form.** Expand the formal 3 × 3 determinant whose first row is i, j, k; the middle component carries a minus sign.
**Anti-commutative.** b × a = −(a × b), and a × a = 0; parallel non-zero vectors have a zero cross product.
**Area.** |a × b| is the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b, so the area of triangle ABC is ½|AB × AC|.
**Exam caution.** Dot the result with both a and b as a one-line check; a sign error in the j component is the most common mistake.
summary: The cross product a×b is a vector perpendicular to both a and b with magnitude |a||b| sin θ, equal to the area of the parallelogram they span.
